key_insight: Vacancy density dominates the predicted degradation of tungsten’s lattice thermal conductivity, with a step-like transition near 0.05 at.% vacancies followed by saturation.
engineering_relevance: Defect-based conductivity predictions could help assess irradiation-induced heat-removal losses in tungsten plasma-facing components for fusion reactors.
method: Generate irradiation defects using the Creation Relaxation Algorithm.
Use non-equilibrium molecular dynamics to relate local temperature gradients to defect concentrations.
Train machine-learning models to map defect features to lattice thermal conductivity.
evidence_signal: Simulations spanning irradiation doses up to 1.8 canonical displacements per atom show nonlinear, saturating conductivity degradation, with machine learning identifying vacancy density as the dominant structural factor.
watch_item: The study addresses lattice conductivity; assessing total heat transport in reactor tungsten also requires electronic contributions and experimental validation.
paper_title: Atomic-level study of dose-dependent lattice thermal conductivity degradation in irradiated tungsten
